title: Docs truth reconciliation: README status, benchmark-spec hash, sqlite driver decision record
description: Objective: close three measured doc-truth gaps (docs audit 2026-08-09). (1) README status paragraph understates the landed foundation: it names only test infra, evidence primitives and the graph kernel, while the repo also has a durable SQLite event store (pnpm verify:store), bounded-JSON input contracts, the control-room truth kernel and the fairness reference; rewrite the status paragraph to match reality at HEAD without claiming design freeze. (2) Benchmark-spec hash divergence: the design doc pins the benchmark spec at SHA-256 F8B84716... (Fable Revision 3) while docs/plans/2026-08-07-fable-fairness-aging-reference.md pins A62B9043...; determine which revision is current and record the resolution in a short docs/plans/ decision note. Do NOT edit the design doc (read-only, outside this repo); if the design-doc side is the stale one, escalate to the human instead. (3) node:sqlite driver: design section 4.1 requires a blocking packaging/fault spike before committing to a driver, but the store was built directly on Node 24 node:sqlite DatabaseSync with no recorded decision; write a retroactive decision record in docs/plans/ capturing the de-facto choice, the evidence in hand (store suite green, 357 tests) and the residual risk (release-candidate API), explicitly awaiting human ratification. NOT in scope: editing the external design doc, code changes. Owned paths: README.md and new files under docs/plans/ only. Verification: content review; pnpm test unaffected.
definitionOfDone: README status paragraph names the actually-landed foundation surfaces at HEAD
benchmark-spec hash divergence resolved in a decision note or explicitly escalated to the human
retroactive node:sqlite decision record exists in docs/plans/ marked as awaiting human ratification

implementationPlan.description: Update only the `## Current status` narrative in `README.md` from the measured repository state. Name the landed durable `SqliteEventStore`/`verify:store` foundation, bounded-JSON contracts, control-room truth-presentation kernel, DEVELOPMENT_ONLY scheduler-fairness reference, and the existing structural graph kernel. Preserve the authority boundary verbatim in substance: this is still provisional/pre-freeze, the fairness model is NOT_CONFIRMATORY, the graph kernel is not execution authority, and none of these surfaces makes the repository a production daemon, proves benchmark superiority, or records design freeze. Do not rewrite commands or unrelated README sections.
implementationPlan.note:
README `## Current status` rewritten from measured HEAD state; Commands block and the Phase 0 evidence-tooling paragraph untouched.

Measured before writing (rail: description claims stale by default), all PRESENT: `packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.ts`, `packages/contracts/src/bounded-json.ts`, `packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts`, `packages/scheduler/src`, `packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/` (17 files). Root scripts confirmed in package.json: `test:store` (line 21), `verify:store` (line 24).

Truth defect avoided: the old sentence "it has no persistence, command, approval, provider, lease, budget, or execution authority" was true of the repo when only the graph kernel existed. With a durable store landed, that clause is now only true SCOPED TO THE KERNEL — so it stays attached to the kernel bullet and was not promoted to a repo-level claim it would have falsified.

Every added surface carries its own non-authority boundary rather than one blanket disclaimer:
- store: refuses below `MINIMUM_SQLITE_VERSION` with the stable code `SQLITE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` (`sqlite-event-store.ts:171-173`, constant `store-contracts.ts:1` = 3.51.3); storage only.
- bounded-JSON: bounds input, says nothing about caller authorization.
- truth kernel: maps provenance to display, cannot upgrade it; UNKNOWN is representable.
- fairness: NOT_CONFIRMATORY, not the production scheduler.

"DEVELOPMENT_ONLY / NOT_CONFIRMATORY" is not my wording — grep confirms it is the fairness reference's own declared status (`docs/plans/2026-08-07-fable-fairness-aging-reference.md:1,4`) and the same literal is pinned in control-room fixtures.

Retained verbatim in substance: provisional pre-freeze, not Phase 1 completion until the six-document Phase 0 manifest and independent `FREEZE_READY`, not a production daemon, not benchmark evidence, no readiness or comparative claim. No freeze is recorded or implied. Forward links to the two step-2/step-3 notes land in the same commit.

implementationPlan.description: Create `docs/plans/2026-08-09-benchmark-spec-hash-resolution.md` as a short decision/escalation record. Record the measured bytes exactly: the read-only design (SHA-256 `1D9D1EC...83191`) names Fable Revision 3 / `F8B84716BFC1FAAB051D698AA9BE353F0D780142D709B7D14496D0B7B65C8885`, while the sole current benchmark artifact declares Revision 4, says it builds on Revision 3, and hashes `A62B90436CC0B911FB28526AF7B7E0F2D1370F6F93DB91C26077F6E2956A589C`; the existing 2026-08-07 fairness reference correctly pins A62. State that Revision 4/A62 is the current available benchmark artifact, but it is untracked in the external `moes` checkout and no freeze/authority upgrade is inferred. Mark resolution `AWAITING_HUMAN_RATIFICATION`, link the general-channel escalation `msg-75308a367d0e4ab5a13b9f3cf6c9a742`, and require the human to reconcile the external design pin or ratify the successor in authoritative freeze evidence. Never edit the external design or benchmark files.

Create `docs/plans/2026-08-09-node-sqlite-driver-decision.md` as a retroactive, non-authoritative decision record with status `PROPOSED — AWAITING HUMAN RATIFICATION`. Capture the de-facto choice (`node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` on pinned Node 24.16.0), current bundled SQLite 3.53.0, the production minimum 3.51.3 and open-time enforcement, `store.health().sqliteVersion`, and the fresh 2026-08-09 evidence `pnpm test:store` => 32 files / 357 tests passing. Cite the Node 24.16.0 official API status as Stability 1.2 / Release candidate. Explicitly document the design-required evidence that is still missing or not equivalent to the local suite: recorded Windows/Linux/macOS packaging qualification, the full Phase-2 crash/fault matrix, and daemon doctor exposure. The proposal may describe continued foundation use pending ratification, but must not claim the skipped blocking spike happened, waive residual risk, or amend the read-only design.

Adversarial truth review across the three owned docs: re-run `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` on both external authority files; inspect the benchmark header and confirm the two decision notes do not swap Revision 3/4, turn current working bytes into freeze authority, or conceal that the benchmark file is untracked; grep production for `DatabaseSync`, `MINIMUM_SQLITE_VERSION`, and `sqliteVersion` and confirm the SQLite note distinguishes implemented local evidence from missing cross-platform/doctor/ratification evidence. Review the README sentence-by-sentence against files that exist on disk, retaining every UNKNOWN/provisional/non-production qualifier. Run `git diff --check` and confirm no external-design edit, generated evidence, or file outside the three owned paths appears.

Final gate only: from `D:\projexts\moe-next`, run exactly `pnpm test:store && pnpm test` in the foreground and record fresh output; if the store count differs from the documented snapshot, update the note truthfully and rerun the same complete command. Then inspect `git status --porcelain`, preserve/unstage all foreign paths, and commit only by explicit pathspec: `git commit -- README.md docs/plans/2026-08-09-benchmark-spec-hash-resolution.md docs/plans/2026-08-09-node-sqlite-driver-decision.md`; verify `git show --stat` contains only those paths.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected editing the authoritative external design because the epic rail makes it read-only and outside task ownership. Rejected silently changing the committed fairness-reference hash back to Revision 3: the only current benchmark artifact explicitly declares Revision 4 and hashes A62, so that would make the local note stale. Rejected calling Revision 4 frozen/normative: the external benchmark file is untracked and the design still pins Revision 3, so only a human can ratify/reconcile the successor. Rejected portraying the landed store suite as the design-mandated packaging/fault spike: it is useful evidence but does not establish cross-platform packaging, the full crash matrix, or doctor integration. Documentation-only scope consciously omits TDD because no behavior changes; the final store/root suites guard against accidental collateral changes.

External `Get-FileHash` measured design SHA-256 `1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191` and benchmark SHA-256 `A62B90436CC0B911FB28526AF7B7E0F2D1370F6F93DB91C26077F6E2956A589C`; benchmark header says Revision 4, builds on Revision 3, while design line 12 pins Revision 3/F8. `git -C D:/projexts/moes status` reports the benchmark file untracked, so no Git lineage is available. planningNotes.risks: The largest risk is converting a measured working-tree fact into authority: Revision 4/A62 is current on disk but untracked, so the note must remain an escalation awaiting human ratification. README expansion can overstate maturity; preserve explicit provisional, non-production, non-benchmark, and non-freeze qualifiers. The SQLite record is retroactive and cannot fabricate the blocking packaging/fault spike; separate the 357-test local Windows evidence from still-missing cross-platform, crash-matrix, and doctor evidence. Shared-tree discipline still applies to docs: commit only the three exact owned paths and never touch the external `moes` files.
